questions.stem: What happens to the resistance of a thermistor as its temperature increases?
questions.explanation: For a typical NTC (negative temperature coefficient) thermistor, resistance decreases as temperature increases. Higher temperatures give more electrons enough energy to become free charge carriers, increasing conductivity.

questions.stem: Which of the following would decrease the resistance of a copper wire?

options.text: Making the wire thicker (larger cross-sectional area)

questions.explanation: Increasing the cross-sectional area of a wire decreases its resistance because there is more space for electrons to flow through. Resistance is inversely proportional to cross-sectional area.
